assessment: This important work by Malita et al. describes a mechanism by which an intestinal inflammatory response causes an increase in daytime sleep through signaling from the gut to the blood-brain barrier. Their findings suggest that cytokines Upd3 and Upd2 produced by the intestine following inflammation act on glia of the blood brain barrier to regulate sleep by modulating Allatostatin A signaling. The evidence is compelling and elegantly performed using the ample Drosophila genetic toolbox, making this work appealing for a broad group of neuroscience researchers interested in sleep and gut-brain interactions.
